title: A DQMC study of the spectral and conductive properties of the two-dimensional Holstein model
authors: J. Neuhaus, B. Cohen-Stead, N. Mannella, S. Johnston
abstract: We study the dynamical properties of the two-dimensional square lattice Holstein Hamiltonian using numerically exact determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations. In particular, we report systematic calculations of the model's single-particle spectral function and optical conductivity over a range of phonon energies, electron-phonon coupling strengths, carrier concentrations, and temperatures. In doing so, we map the evolution of the system from a dressed metallic phase to a (bi)polaron liquid/insulator to a charge-density-wave insulator as the carrier concentration is tuned from dilute values to half-filling. We corroborate these results using several equal-time correlation measurements and related proxy quantities reconstructed from time-displaced correlation measurements. This paper is also accompanied by an extensive open data set, covering over 16,640 unique parameter values.
summary: This paper uses advanced Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to study the two-dimensional Holstein model. It maps the system's behavior as doping changes, revealing transitions between metallic, polaron liquid, and charge-density-wave insulating phases. The work provides detailed spectral and conductive signatures of these correlated electronic states.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamical properties of the two-dimensional Holstein model, specifically mapping the phase evolution as carrier concentration is tuned.
main_result: The analysis characterizes transitions from a dressed metallic phase through (bi)polaron liquid/insulator states to a charge-density-wave (CDW) insulator.
method: The research employs numerically exact Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations, requiring advanced analytic continuation techniques (DEAC/MaxEnt) to extract real-frequency observables.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional square lattice Holstein Hamiltonian, which describes the coupling between itinerant electrons and lattice phonons. The Hamiltonian includes terms for hopping, electron-phonon coupling, and lattice dynamics.
key_observables: Single-particle spectral function A(k, omega), optical conductivity sigma(omega), and charge/spin structure factors Sc(Q) and Ss(q).
important_parameters: Phonon energies, electron-phonon coupling strengths, carrier concentrations (doping), and temperature, studied across over 16,640 parameter values.
main_assumptions: The use of DQMC is numerically exact but relies on complex analytic continuation methods (DEAC/MaxEnt) to bridge imaginary-time simulation data to real-frequency spectra.
figures_summary: The figures likely show the evolution of spectral weight, the opening of gaps in the spectral function, and the suppression of the Drude response in the optical conductivity as CDW order sets in.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the model across various parameter regimes, first establishing the theoretical framework using DQMC, then calculating key observables like the spectral function and conductivity, and finally mapping the phase diagram based on doping and coupling strength.
why_interesting: The study provides detailed, unbiased numerical results for a canonical model (Holstein) that captures the interplay between electronic correlations and lattice degrees of freedom, which is central to understanding high-Tc superconductivity and polaronic physics.
